slides.0.title: Regulation in Depth and Label Reading
slides.0.subtitle: Using names and terms precisely
slides.1.title: PDO/PGI requirements, consolidated
slides.1.highlights.0.title: PDO
slides.1.highlights.0.content: 100% of grapes from the zone; vinified by wineries located in the zone; 33 registered
slides.1.highlights.1.title: PGI
slides.1.highlights.1.content: At least 85% of grapes from the zone, the rest from elsewhere in Greece; only one production stage must occur in the zone; about 114, at Regional (8), District (37) and Area levels
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Share of production
slides.1.highlights.2.content: PDO and PGI together make up only about a third of Greek output, versus over 80% in other EU producers (2022–23 data)
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Declassification routes
slides.1.highlights.3.content: e.g. a Naoussa with another grape falls to Imathia PGI or Macedonia PGI
slides.1.content: A common error is calling PGI "table wine of a region". It is a protected geographical indication with three levels.
slides.2.title: Ageing terms: the pattern and the exceptions
slides.2.highlights.0.title: The general pattern (consistent across materials and Naoussa rules)
slides.2.highlights.0.content: White Reserve: 2 years in total (at least 6 months oak + 6 months bottle); red Reserve: 3 years in total (oak at least 6 months); Grand Reserve: white 3 years, red 4 years
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Naoussa example
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Standard: at least 1 year in oak; Reserve: at least 3 years in total; Grand Reserve: at least 48 months in total (24 oak + 24 bottle)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Exception: Mavrodaphne of Patras
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Its own scale: at least 1 year in oak; Reserve 2 years in oak plus 1 in bottle; Grand Reserve 7 years in total
slides.2.highlights.3.title: Where personal notes differ
slides.2.highlights.3.content: Some older notes give different figures (e.g. 1 year for white Reserve), possibly from an older regime or different basis; confirm against the official product specification before exam answers
slides.2.content: Practice: state the general rule, then the exceptions, then name your source; this is the safe way to cite rules.
slides.3.title: Spellings and easily confused names
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Amyndeo / Amyntaio / Amynteo
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Different transliterations of one appellation; pick one and use it consistently
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Lemnos / Limnos
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Official pages use Limnos while teaching materials mostly use Lemnos
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Savatiano / Savvatiano
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Two spellings of the same grape
slides.3.highlights.3.title: Mavrodaphne / Mavrodafni
slides.3.highlights.3.content: Two spellings of the same grape; the PDO name is Mavrodaphne of Patras
slides.3.content: In Diploma answers consistency matters more than which spelling you pick; add the alternative in brackets if needed.
slides.4.title: Verifying the current lists
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Official sources
slides.4.highlights.0.content: The Greek Ministry of Rural Development and Food and the EU eAmbrosia database
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Promotion body
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Wines of Greece publishes PDO pages summarising grapes, styles and rules
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Mind the date of the source
slides.4.highlights.2.content: For example a 2018 course text lists 28 PDOs against 33 today; always give the year when citing figures
slides.4.content: Rule: check the official source first and the textbook second; if they differ, answer with the official figure and state the year.
slides.5.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
What is the Grand Reserve rule for Mavrodaphne of Patras?
D. Identical to all other reds
It has its own scale, different from the general PDO pattern.
What are the three levels of PGI?
There are 8 Regional and 37 District zones, plus smaller Areas.
If a textbook figure differs from the official one, the safest approach is…
A. use the official figure and state the year
PDO counts are an example: 28 in a 2018 text, 33 today.
